interpreter.failureReason: Interpreter is ~7.7x slower than optimizing-JIT. After 2 hours, the guest had not progressed past GRUB. Full boot would require an estimated 8+ hours.
interpreter.notes: Interpreter is not viable for full x86 guest boot. Useful only for unit tests and conformance.

baseline-jit.failureReason: RPC /bin/true timed out after 340s subprocess timeout (300s RPC client timeout + 30s grace). The baseline-JIT is ~3.5x slower than optimizing-JIT for handshake (57.6s vs 16.5s). The RPC would require an estimated 765s, far exceeding the 300s timeout.
baseline-jit.notes: Baseline-JIT can boot and reach agent bind-ready, and can complete the agent handshake, but is too slow to service RPC exec requests within the 300s timeout.

optimizing-jit.notes: Only tier that completes the full end-to-end path: boot, bind-ready, handshake, and /bin/true RPC.

bootProgress.baseline_jit: Reached bind-ready in ~56 min (3361s observer elapsed including probe retries)

rpcViability.interpreter: RPC not attempted (guest did not reach bind-ready)

qualification: preview/developer-ID evidence; not production release qualification
conclusion: Only the optimizing-JIT tier completes the full x86 guest-agent RPC path within practical timeouts. The baseline-JIT tier boots and handshakes but cannot service RPCs within 300s. The interpreter tier cannot boot a full Linux guest in practical time. The optimizing-JIT tier is the minimum viable execution tier for DoryPC x86 guest-agent workloads.
